regime.headline: U.S. yields remain high while HY spreads have widened sharply—selective credit stress amid lower modelled term premium.
regime.answer: Nominal 10Y ~5.15% with 10Y real ~2.78% and NY Fed ACM term premium down to ~0.76%, while US high‑yield OAS widened ~63bp over 20 sessions versus an ~8bp IG change—signalling selective HY pressure, not broad IG stress; MOVE and intraday fed‑funds evidence are missing and would change the assessment.
regime.implication: Policy‑sensitive yields are sustaining a tighter financing backdrop while credit stress looks concentrated in HY; that raises conditional downside risk to cyclical/levered credits but does not yet confirm a broad risk‑off.
regime.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical MOVE/Treasury‑volatility and intraday fed‑funds‑futures + 2Y/10Y 5m–30m bars for Oct 14–16 showing either persistence or rapid reversion; auction‑flow persistence would also alter the regime call.

stories.title: High‑yield spreads have widened sharply while IG stayed muted.
stories.whatChanged: 20‑session HY OAS expansion (~63bp) versus IG OAS (~8bp) indicates selective stress in lower‑credit buckets over the past month.
stories.whyItMatters: Selective HY widening can raise funding costs for levered issuers and amplify downside for cyclical/AI‑capex exposure without yet proving a broad credit breakdown.
stories.mechanism: Higher yields and funding sensitivity raise rollover/refinancing risk for lower‑quality issuers, leading to HY spread widening; IG resilience limits claims of systemic credit stress.
stories.conclusion: HY is signalling concentrated spread stress while IG remains relatively contained; monitor whether HY widening persists and whether IG/ MOVE begin widening.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Canonical HY/IG daily OAS persistence beyond the 20‑session window and a rising MOVE index or auction‑flow signs of weak absorption would convert this to broad credit stress.

stories.title: Nominal 10Y is high but ACM term premium has fallen; real yields account for much of the level.
stories.whatChanged: NY Fed ACM 10Y term premium fell ~16.4bp to ~0.756% while 10Y nominal remains ~5.15% and real yields are elevated (~2.78%).
stories.whyItMatters: A lower modelled term premium alongside high real yields suggests nominal yields are being driven more by real rate pressure than term‑premium expansion, affecting policy vs long‑end interpretations.
stories.mechanism: Real‑rate strength (higher real yields) pushes nominal yields up even as term premium moderates; without MOVE or full decomposition, the residual attribution is unresolved.
stories.conclusion: Current canonical evidence supports a decomposition where real yields explain much of nominal 10Y while the modelled term premium fell; MOVE and volatility data are required to close the decomposition.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: A canonical MOVE rise or auction sequencing showing persistent stops/tails implying dealer stress would increase the term‑premium/residual contribution and change this story.

investigations.currentExplanation: Front end remains elevated (US 2Y 4.77%) while ACM term premium fell; absence of canonical intraday fed‑funds‑futures and MOVE prevents proving persistence versus a transient spike.

verified.detail: Nvidia and Apple together accounted for more than 15% of the S&P 500, reinforcing the concentration risk behind an index that can remain firm even when participation is weaker.

verified.detail: Saudi-led coalition forces said six Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted on 24 September, with Yanbu among the targeted areas; the report also described claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.title: META Muse catalyst verified
verified.detail: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent and said it planned integration with smart glasses, independently confirming the product catalyst behind the creator's META discussion.

verified.title: RKLB defence-space catalyst verified
verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.
